- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.2) or neutral, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to align with mean reversion bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model overreacts and forecasts overshoot; cap forecast at +2–4% above recent peak.
- Model consistently underestimates in 30-day horizon when sentiment is mixed (0.2–0.6); apply upward bias of 0.5–1.5% to compensate.
- If sentiment history shows repeated short-term reversals (e.g., 2+ swings in 5 days), model fails to capture mean reversion; adjust forecast to align with 10–15-day moving average.
- When sentiment is high but price is flat or declining, model overcorrects; reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid “sentiment-driven overbought” trap.
- For 30-day forecasts, if model’s first 5 days are significantly above true outcome, apply downward correction to later days (especially days 10–15) to reflect lagged momentum.
